“Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns” (RecSys 2025) shows that random history shuffling confounds behavioral order with item availability. Its constrained shuffle prevents interactions from preceding an item’s first observed appearance; across datasets, apparent sequential signal can reflect behavior, availability, or both. First appearance is an availability proxy, not a verified release date. This supports comparing original, randomly shuffled, and availability-constrained histories as diagnostic controls. [Paper](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/)

Graph null models require distinguishing degree from strength: directed degree-preserving swaps retain numbers of distinct incoming/outgoing neighbors, but do not automatically preserve weighted transition counts. Naive accept-all swaps can also produce biased samples. For transition-frequency controls, preserve incoming/outgoing strengths explicitly and verify preserved quantities; preserving degree alone leaves popularity confounding unresolved. [Directed randomization research](https://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.85.046103), [weighted null-model research](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep02729.pdf)

Practical synthesis: compare directed transitions against destination popularity, reversed transitions, and strength-preserving randomized graphs, with availability constraints where feasible. For training diagnostics, subtract the queried user’s entire contribution from transition counts and popularity totals before scoring that user; this reduces self-counting but remains an explanatory diagnostic, not generalization evidence. Select changes using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 protocol. Report the 20-user full-catalog recommendations separately: sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog metrics, so the two settings are not interchangeable. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)
